mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (registered business licence and company registration certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), district-level Market Supervision Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only for Apostille Convention member states: notarize before a Chinese notary, then apply to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China for an apostille. Consular Legalization route only for non-member states: notarize before a Chinese notary, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then obtain consular legalization from the destination state's embassy or consulate. The two routes are parallel, mutually exclusive, and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Business Registration Record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only for Apostille Convention member states: notarization followed by apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China. Consular Legalization route only for non-member states: notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then destination consulate legalization. No sequential combination of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the CN_JV_LTD Chinese joint venture, notarized by a licensed Chinese notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention member states: Chinese notarization plus Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille. For non-member states: Chinese notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, and destination consular legalization. Select only the route that corresponds to the receiving state; never chain apostille and consular legalization on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders' meeting and board of directors of the joint venture, registered with SAMR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention member state route: notarize the consented Articles, then obtain a Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille. Non-member state route: notarize, then obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization followed by consular legalization at the destination embassy or consulate. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in China maintaining the joint venture's proposed or existing account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: notarized bank reference letter plus Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille. For non-member states: notarized bank reference letter, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then consular legalization by the destination state. Use only one mutually exclusive authentication route; do not apply apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every legal person shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, director, senior manager, and authorized signatory must be screened before incorporation and on a continuous, event-driven basis against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, China's domestic sanctions list announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and PBOC suspicious transaction and money-laundering risk databases. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including domestic and foreign PEPs and their family members and close associates, must be classified as higher risk and require enhanced due diligence, source of funds evidence, source of wealth evidence, and senior management approval before relationship establishment. The Global EOR staffing platform must also screen all contractual counterparties, payroll recipients, and intermediary payment rails such as Wise before each payroll cycle to ensure no sanctioned entities, shell-company indicators, negative media, adverse financial integrity flags, or PEP-linked concealed control remain undisclosed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Online Enterprise Name Self-Declaration System and National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chinese enterprise name must be composed exclusively in standardized Chinese characters and must follow the statutory four-tier naming convention: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or operation characteristics, and legal form suffix. The foreign investor's name may be transliterated phonetically into Chinese characters, but Roman letters, Arabic numerals, and non-Chinese scripts are not permitted in the first-tier Chinese name. An English parallel name may be separately recorded for banking and cross-border purposes but is not legally constitutive. The name must not violate social morality, mislead the public, exceed the registered business scope, or create unfair competition with existing protected names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days after a name rejection notice is issued, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the next higher SAMR authority, attaching the official rejection decision, the exact proposed Chinese name, the four-tier name breakdown, the foreign investor's incorporation certificate, and a legal explanation of why the name complies with the Measures for Administration of Enterprise Name Registration. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may commence administrative litigation before the competent People's Court within six months of the reconsideration decision. The reviewing authority must issue a written decision within 30 days of a complete appeal filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox arrangements are generally not permissible for a Sino-foreign equity joint venture engaged in Global Employer of Record and cross-border payroll services. Chinese tax authorities, social security authorities, and commercial banks require an actual leased business premises in the registered district for labour dispatch licence supervision, payroll and social insurance registration, corporate income tax filing, VAT invoice management, and PBOC anti-money laundering customer due diligence. A virtual address will likely be rejected during bank account opening for payroll direct debit or Wise integration, and may trigger adverse findings during municipal tax and market regulation inspections. Consequently, a physical office lease contract and right-to-use documentation are mandatory to evidence commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) physical signage matching the SAMR-registered Chinese name; (2) office lease and rental payment records; (3) staffing presence at the registered address during business hours; (4) labour dispatch administrative licence and payroll records; (5) statutory books, chop, Articles of Association, and tax registration certificates; (6) evidence that the registered office is not a mere mail-forwarding facility. Quantified risk: High, approximately 70% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax authorities or SAMR within the first two years for an EOR/labour-dispatch entity, with materially higher risk during licence renewal, payroll tax audits, or social insurance contribution investigations.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration of the jurisdiction where the registered office is located.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for ordinary incorporation: the PRC Company Law does not impose a minimum registered capital or a blocked escrow account for a standard limited liability company. Shareholders must subscribe their capital and make payment within five years of incorporation pursuant to Article 47 of the Company Law. However, because the Company operates as an Employer of Record and staffing agency, the later application for the Labor Dispatch Administrative License will require registered capital of not less than RMB 2,000,000 and will call for proof of paid-in capital or verified ability to perform dispatch obligations; no blocked escrow account is required by the registry.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, together with the local competent tax authority for the registered address of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Ltd; the official electronic filing system is the Electronic Tax Bureau (eTax) operated by STA, and the national invoice system is the VAT Invoice Management System with the Electronic Invoice Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The statutory tax identifier for a Chinese registered Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is the 18-character Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under the multi-certificate integration system; no separate TIN certificate is issued. The JV must complete tax registration at the competent local STA office within 30 days of obtaining its business license; the USCC is automatically synchronized to the STA via the SAMR registration data feed. For the foreign non-resident joint-venture partner that has no permanent establishment in China, the partner must obtain a non-resident enterprise taxpayer identification number through the JV as the statutory withholding agent by submitting the home-country certificate of incorporation, board resolution, and power of attorney appointing the JV as its tax agent; the TIN is recorded in the STA tax collection and management system before any dividend or interest remittance is made. For EOR/payroll operations, the JV must additionally register as an Individual Income Tax withholding employer on the eTax portal and create the payroll withholding tax account linked to the same USCC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists in China. Available statutory elections relevant to the JV are: (1) election to be taxed as a general VAT taxpayer as soon as the unified social credit code is obtained, regardless of the RMB 5 million turnover threshold, in order to claim input VAT credits; (2) for labour dispatch and EOR services, the general VAT taxpayer may elect the deemed-cost deduction (difference) method with VAT charged at 5%, or the ordinary 6% rate on gross service fees; (3) a non-resident enterprise without books and records may elect the deemed profit method, at the approval of the STA, instead of actual taxable income calculation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The general VAT taxpayer mandatory registration threshold is RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable turnover; the JV must nevertheless complete regular tax registration immediately upon incorporation, and can voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer even below the threshold. VAT-exemption thresholds for small-scale taxpayers apply only to qualifying small periodic sales and do not exempt a licensed EOR entity from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a real-time fiscal invoice clearance system under the VAT Invoice Management System and the Electronic Invoice Service Platform. VAT invoices must be issued through STA-approved electronic invoice software using taxpayer digital certificates (UKey/electronic signature); every invoice is validated, encrypted, electronically signed and stamped by the STA before delivery to the counterparty. The issuer must transmit line-item data, commodity/service tax classification codes, amounts, and buyer Unified Social Credit Code in prescribed schema through the platform application programming interface. Buyers must authenticate digital e-invoices in the VAT Invoice Comprehensive Service Platform before claiming input VAT. Red-letter (credit note) invoices require pre-approval through the platform, and mismatch/exception management is automated under the anti-fraud digital stamping controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods are subject to the zero rate and eligible for export VAT rebate when they physically depart from mainland China and the export is verified by China Customs. Cross-border services supplied by the EOR company to an overseas recipient may be zero-rated or VAT-exempt under the cross-border taxable services rules only where the recipient is a non-resident, the service is rendered to and consumed wholly outside mainland China, and the remuneration is paid from outside China and repatriated through official banking channels. Staffing/Employment-of-Record services performed inside China or in support of a domestic establishment will not qualify for zero rating and will be taxable at 6% (or 5% under the simplified labour-dispatch difference method).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) - China Customs export goods declaration with release/export customs database number
Bill of Lading (or air waybill for air freight) evidencing export movement and overseas destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / bank foreign exchange settlement receipt evidencing overseas client payment and repatriation
Export sales invoice and, for goods, the input VAT special invoices supporting the export rebate calculation

Cross-border service agreement, service performance/consumption-outside-China evidence, and certification that the overseas recipient has no Chinese permanent establishment (for zero-rated services in lieu of customs clearance)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA data-mines export data from China Customs, State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) foreign exchange collection monitoring, and VAT invoice data. If zero-rating is claimed without proof of physical export, foreign performance, or FX repatriation, the STA will claw back VAT refunded/not collected, add daily late-payment surcharge, and impose an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under the Tax Collection Administration Law. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day window or obtain an approved extension causes the export to be recharacterized as domestic taxable supply. Fraudulent export tax refund claims are criminal under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and can result in repayment, criminal fines, confiscation, and imprisonment; the statutory recovery limitation period does not apply to fraudulent conduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) / State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a managed foreign exchange regime under which current account transactions are broadly convertible, while capital account transactions remain subject to SAFE registration, verification, and use restrictions. The Sino-foreign Equity Joint Venture will be treated as a resident foreign-invested enterprise, allowing it to open both RMB basic settlement accounts and foreign currency current accounts at domestic banks. Export proceeds are generally current account items and can be freely settled into RMB or retained in foreign currency, provided the underlying customs declarations and service trade documentation are presented to the bank. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted after annual audited financial statements are filed, corporate income tax is duly settled, and a board resolution declaring dividends is submitted to the bank; there is no separate remittance tax, but the enterprise must complete SAFE and tax clearances. Capital injections require SAFE registration before the inbound remittance and a Chinese CPA capital verification report after arrival. The RMB is convertible under the current account for legitimate trade and service payments, but capital account outflows, external borrowing, and cross-border hedging are tightly licensed. The practical effect is full operational flexibility for payroll and trade settlements combined with substantial documentary discipline for shareholder loans, dividends, and capital reductions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from goods must be repatriated into China within 180 days from the customs declaration date unless SAFE grants an approved extension. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into RMB; the JV may retain the full amount in a foreign currency current account or voluntarily settle into RMB through the bank's verification system. All export receipts must be matched against electronic customs declarations through SAFE's goods trade monitoring system before being credited, and any netting or write-off requires a formal SAFE approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign fintech electronic money institutions, including Wise and other digital EMI platforms, are not licensed as deposit-taking banks in mainland China and cannot maintain a primary treasury account or provide domestic RMB clearing for a registered Sino-foreign JV. Such EMIs are legally barred from offering onshore settlement, capital-account custody, or FX hedging services directly. Their practical viability is limited to side-coordination for low-value offshore contractor payouts or employee travel cards, routed through PBOC-licensed cross-border payment partners, but they cannot replace a domestic Tier-1 bank account for statutory capital, payroll compliance, tax payments, or annual FX reporting. The treasury blueprint must therefore place 100% of formal banking on domestic banks and treat fintech rails only as a last-mile convenience where a regulated Chinese licensed payment institution carries the transaction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative, or a clearly authorized senior manager holding a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, must appear physically in-branch to complete the account-opening interview under PBoC counter-terrorism and AML rules. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted by Chinese Tier-1 banks for the primary operating accounts; a video interview with the appointed deputy may be accepted by a few banks after the power of attorney is authenticated. Statutory directors who are not legal representatives do not need to attend, but the bank will require their identification documents, board resolutions, and, in practice, expect at least one resident director with signing authority to be physically available during onboarding and subsequent high-risk account changes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The EOR and contractor payroll model produces large recurring outbound payments to multiple overseas beneficiaries that may resemble invoice laundering or pass-through financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EOR service agreements with each client; employer-of-record agreements with each overseas contractor; monthly payroll ledger showing gross-to-net calculations; social security and tax withholding records; invoices showing the mark-up as a genuine service fee; bank payment instruction logs tied to the payroll ledger; and a documented three-way reconciliation between client purchase order, EOR service agreement, and payroll disbursement list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and ownership opacity if the joint venture parent holds its interest through offshore special purpose vehicles or a multi-tier trust chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAMR business registration extract for every entity in the ownership chain; notarized trust deeds and declarations of trust; identity documents for every natural person with 10% or more direct or indirect ownership; a legal opinion from a Chinese law firm confirming beneficial ownership; source of wealth and source of funds evidence for capital contributors; and audited financial statements of the material parent entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk counterparty exposure, particularly when remote contractors reside in sanctioned jurisdictions or the client portfolio includes politically exposed persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated OFAC, EU, UN, and Chinese sanctions screening outputs for the full client and contractor book; enhanced due diligence files for every high-risk jurisdiction; negative news and adverse media search documentation; a written sanctions compliance policy applicable to the JV; a senior AML officer nomination; and a transaction monitoring summary showing no red-flag activity across selected historical flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mischaracterization of foreign exchange purpose, including attempts to use capital-account funds for current-account payroll or to circumvent SAFE's payment purpose coding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration certificate; board resolutions approving the specific capital injection purpose; CPA capital verification report; separate bank sub-accounts for capital and operational payroll; a funds usage runbook demonstrating that registered capital is only deployed for approved operating expenditures; and a complete SAFE current-account payment application pack with service/service-outcome invoices, payroll runbooks, and counterparty due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injection wires must be routed through a SAFE-registered domestic bank using SWIFT MT103 or MT103 plus MT202 cover, with the payment description clearly citing the SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration number and the purpose code for inbound direct investment capital injection. The receiving bank will verify the funds against the FDI registration and thereafter issue a bank slip confirming entry into the Capital Escrow Account. A Chinese CPA must subsequently issue a capital verification report confirming the paid-in capital. The JV may then settle the foreign currency into RMB via the bank's capital settlement system, subject to SAFE's negative list, and must not apply the funds to speculative investments, equity purchases, or unauthorized outbound lending.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For global EOR payroll and contractor settlements, the primary clearing rail is bank-integrated SWIFT MT103 for high-value cross-border wires, supplemented by domestic batch direct debit rails for onshore payroll and CIPS for cross-border RMB leg payments. For trade-related procurement or settlement, Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections remain acceptable where underlying shipment and service documents exist, but the EOR will typically use simple service-trade MT103 payments with purpose codes validated by invoices and work completion evidence. All outbound payments must pass the bank's transaction monitoring system and be traceable to the payroll ledger or service agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore calendar and non-deliverable forward contracts written by a Chinese licensed bank with SAFE-verified underlying current-account exposure, maximum tenor generally aligned to the invoice maturity
Bank-customer FX options on a trade and service income background, limited to cost-bearing structures and SAFE registration
Cross-currency swaps between USD and RMB approved by SAFE for matched long-term capital account liability or asset positions
Offshore NDF contracts are not permissible for the domestic JV as direct counterparty; only offshore group entities may access offshore NDF markets, and any onshore settlement must be prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; administered by the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June for the immediately preceding financial year ending 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June results in the company being placed on the Operating Abnormalities Directory within 10 working days. Uninterrupted non-compliance for 3 consecutive years triggers inclusion in the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, public credit restriction, restrictions on bank and government transactions, and eventual administrative revocation of the business license or strike-off of registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Reconciliation Return and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the local Tax Service Bureau or electronic tax bureau.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 31 May of the following financial year for the calendar year ended 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax. Non-filing of the annual return triggers a fine of RMB 200 to RMB 2,000 in ordinary cases, rising to RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for materially serious cases; understating taxable income attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, plus asset preservation, bank freeze and business enforcement action by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce and local commerce commissions, jointly collected through SAMR, the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, and the Foreign Investment Information System.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June; reports foreign shareholders, actual controllers, investment amounts and changes as at 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or knowingly false reporting triggers a rectification order from the commerce authority; refusal to rectify is recorded on the enterprise credit record and may lead to administrative fines, restrictions on foreign-exchange payment transactions, and disqualification from preferential foreign-investment measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Labor Dispatch Administrative License Annual Operation Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) through the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau that issued the labor dispatch license.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for the preceding calendar year; this is a mandatory condition for retaining a valid labor dispatch and employer-of-record license.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false annual reporting causes the license-issuing authority to mark the agency non-compliant, impose administrative fines, refuse annual license renewal, and ultimately revoke the Labor Dispatch Administrative License; revocation makes continued EOR or staffing operation unlawful in China.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Accounts Approval and Chinese CPA Audit File
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders and board for internal adoption; CPA audit opinion retained in the statutory corporate book; audited accounts submitted with the EIT annual filing package to STA and used in the SAMR annual credit report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements must be prepared for the calendar year and audited before the 31 May EIT reconciliation due date; shareholder approval and filing of the approved audit report in corporate records must be completed by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Audit omissions violate the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law, leading to orders requiring correction, fines against the company and responsible persons, and treatment of the annual EIT return and annual credit report as defective; repeated failure may lead to credit penalties and revocation of market-participation permits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, every Chinese company, irrespective of balance-sheet size, turnover, headcount or profitability, must prepare an annual financial report and have it audited by an accounting firm with Chinese CPAs. There is no small-company exempt threshold; any positive balance-sheet, any turnover and any employee headcount are sufficient to trigger the statutory audit. Additional mandatory audit designation rules apply to the labor-dispatch and EOR licence, which requires an annual audit-compliant financial report to support licence annual review; public, listed, banking, insurance and State-owned companies are subject to further quantitative triggers under sectoral regulations, including asset and revenue thresholds requiring expanded audit certification for regulated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Law and the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law; financial statements must be prepared under Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises, which are substantially converged with IFRS; small-scale enterprises may apply the Basic Standard for Small Enterprises; tax-filing financial statements must follow PRC GAAP and cannot use unaudited foreign GAAP without a signed Chinese CPA audit report.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: PRC law does not require a standalone annual UBO return; the company must maintain an internal register identifying its beneficial owners, controlling shareholders and actual controllers. The annual credit report, Foreign Investment Annual Information Report and Labor Dispatch Annual Operation Report collectively re-confirm the ultimate controlling investor, actual controller and 31 December shareholding profile. Any shareholding transfer or change in actual controller must be documented in the corporate registers and filed with SAMR or the local Market Supervision Administration within 30 days of the change; the 30-day event window is mandatory and no annual amnesty exists.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors, Supervisors and Senior Management
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Equity Pledges
Minute Book and Board/Shareholder Resolution File
Register of Legal Representative and Company Seal Usage

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 to USD 1,500 per annum for a registered office address and local corporate agent or secretarial support in a tier-1 Chinese city; higher in premium commercial districts.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 to USD 5,000 per annum for a small EOR or joint venture with standard payroll operations; a multinational consolidated audit or regulatory-format audit can exceed USD 10,000 per annum.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard China Mainland Corporate Income Tax rate is 25%. A reduced 15% CIT rate applies to qualifying New/High-Technology Enterprises with registered 'core intellectual property' and qualifying R&D expenditure, to qualified strategic emerging software enterprises, and to qualifying encouraged industries in the Western Regions. Additional incentives include super-deduction of 175%-200% (currently 100% temporary uplift for qualifying R&D expenses) and 10-year loss carryforward only for qualified high-tech enterprises under specific grace rules. No patent box regime exists for passive holding or shell JVs; free-zone preferential treatment requires substantive business operations and is not available to an EOR JV that merely invoices global contractor fees without local economic substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A) — the unified A-class CIT annual return — filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (China e-Tax / Electronic Taxpayer System). Supporting schedules include A105000 Tax Adjustment Schedule, A105050 Employee Compensation and Benefits, A105080 Fixed Assets, A108000 Foreign Tax Credit Schedule, and A107012 R&D Incentive Schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final filing with quarterly provisional CIT prepayments during the taxable year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final annual CIT return must be filed and self-assessed within five months after the financial year-end, i.e., no later than 31 May of the following calendar year. Quarterly prepayments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter, and the final balance is due with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross operating revenue from global EOR, staffing, payroll administration, contractor payment settlement, and related service commissions. Exclude output VAT and VAT-exclusive invoiced amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Sino-foreign Equity Joint Venture with Chinese resident status, include all worldwide revenue, including fees received from overseas group entities for offshore contractor payroll administration. Do not net cross-border subcontractor payroll unless the JV is the legally disclosed agent. Reconcile reported revenue to VAT issuance records, bank receipts, and Wise/local payroll payment rails. If foreign-source services are performed outside China, preserve evidence of the service location and invoice chain to support possible foreign tax credit claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report direct cost of EOR services: employee wages, social insurance, housing fund, payroll agency costs, subcontract labor, direct contractor settlement costs, communication systems, and onboarding compliance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only wages paid to actual Chinese employees subject to Individual Income Tax withholding and social insurance contributions. Payments to overseas contractors or foreign hiring entities are not deductible as wages; treat them as intercompany service costs and require valid invoices, enforceable contracts, and proof that services were rendered. Any excessive or non-arm’s-length cross-border subcontracting fee must be adjusted in transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 — Management and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report selling, marketing, external professional fees, rent, IT systems, banking charges, exchange losses, and intercompany management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees allocated from a foreign parent are deductible only when accompanied by a written service agreement, actual benefit evidence, cost allocation methodologies, and contemporaneous documentation. Non-resident related parties receiving management or technical fees must be paid net of China withholding tax unless treaty relief is obtained. Add back any parent-company general treasury expenses or group brand charges lacking direct benefit to the Chinese EOR operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report accounting profit before tax prepared under PRC Accounting Standards (or IFRS with required reconciliation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the audited financial statements to the CIT return. Accruals for employee variable compensation, end-of-year bonuses, unpaid withholdings, and dividend withholding tax must be reflected consistently. For cross-border operations, ensure all outbound invoices have been recorded in the correct period and that profit is not artificially reduced by unpaid or shell-invoice liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all taxable income additions and deductions removed from accounting profit, including non-deductible penalties, excessive entertainment expenses, unreported related-party transactions, and R&D super-deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Chinese tax authorities will require add-back of expenses without valid special VAT invoices, expenses not actually paid to commercial substance, excessive donations, fines, and transfer pricing adjustments. Subtract qualified tax-exempt income, notional interest from treasury bonds, and additional R&D super-deductions. A non-resident parent’s strategic outsourcing costs cannot be claimed as Chinese R&D unless personnel, management, and R&D activities are actually performed in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report current-year taxable income offset by prior-year operating tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from overseas branches or foreign related-party service lines cannot be used to offset China-source operating profit unless they arise in the same taxable entity. Losses may be carried forward for five years; unlimited loss carryforward is not available to a standard EOR JV. A change in holding structure or shareholder does not restart the carryforward period, but a reorganization may trigger loss forfeiture.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 20 / Box 21 — Applicable Tax Rate and Preliminary CIT Liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the standard 25% tax rate or a reduced preferential rate to taxable income and compute preliminary CIT liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Sino-foreign Equity Joint Venture established in mainland China is a resident enterprise and is taxed on its worldwide income. Its operating profit is not subject to the non-resident dividend rate; the 10% withholding tax is imposed only when profits are distributed to the foreign shareholder. If the JV qualifies as a High/New-Technology Enterprise or small low-profit enterprise, attach qualification certificates and election schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 24 / Box 25-26 — Final Tax Payable / Prepayments and Balance Dues
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute actual CIT liability after tax incentives and foreign tax credits, offset quarterly prepayments, and report the balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure quarterly prepayments have not been materially understated to avoid interest and penalties on the annual settlement. The final balance must be paid by 31 May. Before remitting any dividend to the foreign JV shareholder, withhold 10% Chinese withholding tax on the gross dividend received from the Chinese JV, unless a lower treaty rate is secured through the Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership application procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total wages and salaries, bonus accruals, welfare contributions, training costs, labor union funds, and social insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the JV operates as an Employer of Record, every payroll dollar must match a real employment agreement, PRC individual income tax filing, social insurance payment registration, and bank payroll transfer template. Worldwide contractor payments made to foreign self-employed workers are not employee compensation and cannot be claimed as wages; they must be substantiated as independent contractor service costs with the appropriate service invoice and withholding obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Supporting Schedule A108000 — Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxes paid to foreign tax authorities on foreign-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the foreign tax credit only for taxes paid on income genuinely sourced outside China and subject to Chinese CIT. The credit is capped at the Chinese CIT payable on that foreign income. Maintaining foreign payroll operation tax records and reconciliation schedules is mandatory. Do not claim credit for taxes withheld on Chinese-sourced dividends paid by foreign holding vehicles, as that would duplicate treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return may result in a fine not exceeding CNY 2,000, or CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000 for serious cases, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax. Inaccurate filings that trigger underpayment due to false claims or concealed income are subject to 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under the Tax Collection Administration Law. Where tax evasion exceeds the criminal threshold (typically > CNY 50,000 and > 10% of tax payable), the responsible legal representative and direct officers may be subject to criminal penalties under Criminal Law Article 201, including imprisonment. Deliberately issuing false VAT invoices to support payroll or contractor deductions can trigger the false-invoice criminal regime with penalties up to life imprisonment in the most severe cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding tax rate under a bilateral Double Tax Treaty, the Chinese JV as withholding agent must, before remitting dividends, obtain from the foreign shareholder: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder’s tax authority; (2) a signed beneficial ownership declaration with documentary evidence proving the shareholder is not a conduit or a lack-of-substance shell; and (3) background documentation of ultimate owner, bank confirmation, board minutes authorizing the distribution, and shareholding structure. The withholding agent must file the non-resident tax withholding application and treaty-benefit application with the Chinese tax authority through the electronic Taxpayer System; only after approval may the reduced treaty rate be applied. If approval is not obtained, the full 10% statutory WHT must be withheld and paid. China has also issued anti-treaty-abuse rules under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, and a shareholder without economic substance or core income-generating activities in the treaty jurisdiction will be denied treaty benefits and reassessed at 10% with late fees.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory China WHT on cross-border royalties and interest is 10%, including payments made by the Chinese EOR JV to foreign related parties for software, trademark, platform license, or intercompany debt. Under many China DTA treaties, royalty rates are reduced to 5% to 10%, and interest to 0%, 5%, 7.5%, or 10%, depending on the counterparty jurisdiction and the beneficial-owner status of the recipient. Royalty payments on franchise or outsourcing platform rights require a genuine license, and interest on intercompany loans requires a written loan agreement, arm’s-length interest rate, and proof of actual cash flows. Non-resident income tax and VAT on royalties and interest must be withheld and paid at the time of payment; failure to withhold triggers a 50% to 300% penalty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under China’s contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation rules, a Local File must be prepared if any of the following annual related-party transaction thresholds is met: tangible-property transfers exceeding CNY 200 million; intangible-property transfers exceeding CNY 100 million; financial transactions exceeding CNY 100 million; or other related-party transactions exceeding CNY 40 million. A Master File is required where aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed CNY 1 billion, and Country-by-Country reporting applies when the ultimate parent’s consolidated group revenue is at least CNY 5.5 billion. Even below these thresholds, the JV must complete the related-party transaction reporting schedule within the annual CIT return and must be able to justify all cross-border pricing on demand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime equivalent to Caribbean offshore jurisdictions; however, Chinese tax authorities apply the substance-over-form doctrine, the beneficial ownership test, and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under CIT Law Article 47. For a Global EOR staffing entity, economic substance requires actual contracts, local registered office, employed staff, payroll software systems, board decisions, billing and collections, bank accounts, employment records, and performance of Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in China. A treaty-shopping structure where the foreign shareholder is a pure conduit and the Chinese JV is a thin-capitalized invoice-center with no local personnel is vulnerable to an anti-avoidance recharacterization, denial of treaty relief, and assessment of a 10% WHT plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through Fabricated EOR Payroll And False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or receiving VAT invoices and payroll documentation for workers who are not actual employees of the JV, creating sham employment contracts, backdating timesheets, inflating headcount, or using shell subcontractors to manufacture deductible payroll and service costs for clients without any real Employer of Record employment relationship.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 and Invoice Management Law, false invoicing and fabricated expense deductions constitute tax evasion and false-invoice offenses. The tax authority may disallow all sham deductions, impose a penalty of 50% to 500% of the unpaid CIT and VAT, and levy daily late-payment surcharges. If false special VAT invoices are involved, Criminal Law Article 205 imposes fines and imprisonment from three years up to life imprisonment for the most serious amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct, sign, or fail to prevent forged payroll invoices may have the corporate veil pierced to recover evaded taxes and civil restitution of diverted funds. Responsible persons are subject to exit bans or travel blacklisting orders preventing departure before tax liabilities are settled. Criminal conviction can result in up to seven years’ imprisonment for general tax evasion, or up to life imprisonment for false special VAT invoices, plus confiscation of personal assets and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Shifting And Non-Arm’s-Length Cross-Border Service Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Draining Chinese JV profitability by paying excessive management fees, technology fees, platform access fees, data-processing fees, or marketing commissions to a foreign affiliate or Hong Kong/offshore parent without arm’s-length pricing, actual performance of services, or proper supporting documentation, while retaining no economic substance in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under CIT Law Article 41 and the Special Tax Adjustment Measures, the State Taxation Administration may make a transfer-pricing adjustment, recharacterize the transaction, add interest, and impose a 50% to 200% penalty on the underpaid tax where the taxpayer failed to keep contemporaneous documentation. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule (CIT Law Article 47) allows retroactive reassessment with interest from the transaction year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve fictitious or inflated cross-border fees can be held jointly liable for the Chinese JV’s underpaid tax and to restore assets for creditors. The responsible legal representative may be included in the tax authorities’ major-tax-case blacklist, subject to asset freezes, travel bans, and denial of exit permits. If the profit shifting causes prolonged tax loss beyond the criminal threshold, directors may be prosecuted as accomplices to tax evasion, with imprisonment up to seven years and personal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure To Withhold Non-Resident Dividend, Interest, And Royalty Tax And Improper DTA Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or paying interest and royalties to foreign shareholders and related parties without withholding the statutory 10% Chinese withholding tax, or claiming treaty relief with a shell entity that lacks beneficial ownership, Tax Residency Certificate, or Core Income-Generating Activities, causing China-source tax revenue loss.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 69, the withholding agent (the Chinese JV) is liable to pay the withheld tax that should have been collected and is subject to a fine from 50% to 300% of the unrecovered withholding tax. The tax authority may also deny treaty relief, reassess at the full 10% statutory rate with daily interest at 0.05%, and penalize misstatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize profit distribution or cross-border payments while knowingly ignoring withholding obligations may face personal civil liability for the unpaid withholding tax and interest, and may be subject to exit restrictions and blacklisting until payment is made. Willful non-withholding or fraudulent documentation submitted to secure treaty benefits may constitute tax evasion or fraud, exposing the responsible directors to restitution of corporate assets, travel bans, and imprisonment for up to seven years under criminal tax provisions.
